module_title: PoA 1992, Yashpal Committee & Pedagogical Shifts to NEP 2020
introduction: Tailored for UGC NET and advanced DSSSB exams, this level explores the 1992 modifications to NPE 1986, the burden of rote learning addressed by the Yashpal Committee, and critically contrasts the philosophical shifts from NPE 1986 to the modern NEP 2020.

core_concepts.title: Programme of Action (PoA) 1992
core_concepts.description:
NPE 1986 was reviewed and updated in 1992 under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao. This updated document is known as the Programme of Action (PoA) 1992.
Review Committees:
1. Ramamurti Review Committee (1990): Emphasized the promotion of a more humane and egalitarian educational system, highlighting the need to reduce the academic burden on students.
2. Janardhan Reddy Committee (1992): Provided the final inputs for the PoA.
Key Changes in 1992: Expanded Operation Blackboard to the upper primary level and mandated that 50% of future teacher recruits be women.

core_concepts.title: Yashpal Committee (1993): 'Learning Without Burden'
core_concepts.description:
Though not a full education policy, this report heavily influenced modern Indian pedagogy. Chaired by Prof. Yashpal, the committee investigated the problem of heavy school bags and rote memorization.
Key Findings & Recommendations:
- Academic burden is a symptom of treating information as a finite commodity to be memorized, rather than understanding concepts.
- Recommended that homework for primary classes be completely abolished.
- Stressed that the language of textbooks should be colloquial and relatable to the child's life.

core_concepts.title: NPE 1986 vs. NEP 2020: The Structural & Philosophical Shift
core_concepts.description:
1. Structure: 
   - NPE 1986: 10+2+3 (Ages 6-16 in school, ignoring formal Early Childhood Education in the main structure).
   - NEP 2020: 5+3+3+4 (Ages 3-18, formally bringing ages 3-6 into the fold via ECCE/Anganwadis).
2. Curriculum: 
   - NPE 1986: Rigid separation of streams (Science vs. Commerce vs. Arts) in the +2 stage.
   - NEP 2020: No hard separations between arts and sciences, curricular and extra-curricular. Total flexibility.
3. Assessment: 
   - NPE 1986: Summative, end-of-year, high-stakes board exams.
   - NEP 2020: Formative, competency-based continuous evaluation via the 360-degree Holistic Progress Card (HPC).

core_concepts.title: Work Experience vs. Vocational Education
core_concepts.description: The Kothari Commission introduced 'Work Experience' (participation in productive work). By the time of NPE 1986, this evolved into SUPW (Socially Useful Productive Work). NEP 2020 transforms this entirely into formal 'Vocational Education' starting from Grade 6 (including 10 bagless days for internships).

important_entities.name: Common School System (CSS)
important_entities.key_fact: A highly debated Kothari Commission recommendation that failed to materialize fully.
important_entities.significance: CSS aimed to provide equitable quality education to all children, irrespective of caste, creed, or economic status, in their neighborhood schools. While Kothari and NPE 1986 advocated for it, the proliferation of private elite schools undermined it. The RTE Act 2009 (25% reservation for weaker sections) was a modern attempt to force a mini-CSS model.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners will often list 'NPE 1992' as an option. There is **NO** National Policy on Education 1992. India only had three official NPEs: 1968, 1986, and 2020. What happened in 1992 was merely the **Programme of Action (PoA)**—a modification of the 1986 policy. Always select NPE 1986 if the question asks for the policy base of the 1990s.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Always link Prof. Yashpal with the phrase 'Learning Without Burden' (बिना बोझ के शिक्षा) and the reduction of heavy school bags.

exam_strategy_tips: If an advanced question asks which committee highlighted the issue of treating 'information as knowledge' (rote learning), the answer is the **Yashpal Committee (1993)**. If asked who reviewed NPE 1986 first, it is the **Ramamurti Committee (1990)**.
